name: Pouye
catalog_citation: Dede, Wendy & Dorothea Reuter. 2011. Pouye Grammar Essentials. Ukarumpa: Summer Institute of Linguistics (SIL PNG archive item 62023), 124 pp.
catalog_locator: §2.3 Syllable structure, p. 10 (examples (1)-(2); cross-ref §2.5.6 Labial-velar approximant deletion, p. 17; §3.1.6 Compound Nouns
catalog_quote: Syllable stress most commonly occurs on the penultimate syllable. If wɨ or wo are present in the penultimate position the stress if deferred to an adjacent syllable. (1) /wɨl.ouk/ 'snake' (2) /ka.wo.wi/ 'white' ... [§2.5.6] The suffix –wo 'only' becomes –o when it is in the penultimate position. The syllable stress causes the –wo to become –o, since wo cannot fall in the penultimate position; semantically this suffix is emphasised. If the –wo is the ultimate syllable of a word, and therefore no longer carries the syllable stress, it does not change to –o (see §2.3 Syllable structure). ... [§3.1.6] The stress of the words do not change in the compound.

audit.quote_check: confirmed in the copy we hold
audit.reasoning: (1) Quote check: all three quoted passages are verbatim in the held Dede & Reuter 2011 PDF at the cited sections/pages (p.10 §2.3, p.17 §2.5.6, p.27 §3.1.6; the 'stress if deferred' typo is the source's own). (2) Deciding source is a 2011 SIL 'Grammar Essentials' draft sketch (124 pp, unreviewed), impressionistic and hedged, but it is the only grammar-level description of Pouye that exists per Glottolog (13 refs, 1 grammar sketch) and per the SIL-PNG resource list (2016 capture: OPD, Ferree 2000, this grammar, literacy booklets). (3) The one other phonological source, the SIL Organised Phonology Data sheet (item 42318; Ferree 1992 data), was downloaded: 'Stress is usually either penultimate or antepenultimate, with most being penultimate.' This is consistent with our penultimate-default coding and with Dede & Reuter's antepenultimate example /ˈka.wo.wi/, but it frames antepenultimate stress
